nodes.description: TGCTs are exquisitely sensitive to cisplatin-based chemotherapy due to limited nucleotide excision repair capacity (low ERCC1/XPA/XPF expression), retained wild-type TP53 in most cases enabling a robust apoptotic response, and high expression of pro-apoptotic factors (NOXA, BAX) coupled to pluripotency factor OCT4. Both the death receptor (FAS/FASL) and mitochondrial apoptotic pathways become strongly activated following cisplatin treatment.

nodes.description: DNA methylation and histone modifications are primary determinants of TGCT subtype identity. GCNIS and seminomas exhibit global DNA hypomethylation resembling fetal gonocytes, whereas non-seminomas show progressive lineage-specific hypermethylation: embryonal carcinoma exhibits an ESC-like pluripotency program (OCT4, SOX2, LIN28, NANOG) capable of differentiating into AFP-producing yolk sac tumor, beta-hCG-producing choriocarcinoma, and chemoresistant teratoma.

nodes.description: Nearly all postpubertal (type II) TGCTs arise from germ cell neoplasia in situ (GCNIS, formerly carcinoma in situ or intratubular germ cell neoplasia unclassified). GCNIS cells resemble fetal gonocytes/primordial germ cells that failed to mature normally during embryonic testicular development, supported by germline susceptibility in Sertoli-cell KITLG (stem cell factor) paracrine signaling to KIT-expressing primordial germ cells; they remain dormant within seminiferous tubules until puberty and subsequently accumulate chromosomal abnormalities that drive progression to invasive TGCT.

nodes.description: Activating somatic mutations and amplifications in KIT and KRAS are the most significantly mutated somatic driver events in TGCTs, occurring predominantly in tumors with seminomatous components (KIT mutated in ~18-30% of patients). Gain-of-function KIT mutations increase receptor tyrosine kinase activity, whereas activating KRAS codon-12 substitutions impair intrinsic and GAP-stimulated GTP hydrolysis (decreased GTPase activity), locking KRAS in its active GTP-bound conformation and driving increased RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK and PI3K-AKT signaling.
